title: Deconfounding Game 3: an unobserved confounder and its proxy
content: B confounds the proposed effect of X on Y but cannot be observed. A is an observed consequence of both X and B; adjusting for this proxy neither blocks the true back-door path nor avoids collider bias.

variables.name: Treatment (X)
variables.content: The proposed cause whose effect on Y is sought.

variables.name: Outcome (Y)
variables.content: The outcome caused by X and confounded by B.

variables.name: Unobserved Confounder (B)
variables.content: The unobservable common cause of X and Y.

variables.name: Observed Proxy (A)
variables.content: An observed consequence of both X and B, hence a collider and imperfect proxy.

arrows.because: B is a common cause of treatment X.
A is an observed proxy descended from B.
A is also caused by X, making it a collider.
This is the proposed causal effect.
